curated.instructions: omr/instructions/8001-1-1.pdf (the droid is pages 2-46, its functions shown in photos on pages 47-55; pages 56-82 build a second version and its commander and security colourings)

functions.does: The droid folds up for transport: the legs swing up against the body at the hips, turning round the axle of the 24-tooth gear in the hips, and a catch clicks into the gear to hold them folded.
functions.source: book: hips steps 5-13 (page 6 arrow); photos on pages 47-48 and 50

functions.does: Pressing the round button on the back of the hips tips the lever it sits on, lifting the catch out of the 24-tooth gear so the folded droid can open.
functions.source: book: hips step 6 (the lever with its two round buttons); photo on page 51
functions.note: which end of the lever holds the gear isn't clear from the book: inferred from the photo of the button being pressed

functions.does: Once the catch is lifted, rubber bands round the two pulleys in the hips spring the droid open and stand it up.
functions.source: book: hips steps 12-14 (page 6 arrow); photos on pages 51-52
functions.skip: rubber bands only matter under force

functions.does: The head folds down onto the back for transport and swings back up, pivoting on an axle at the top of the torso.
functions.source: book: photos on pages 49 and 52; torso step 13

functions.does: Turning the grey gear on the backpack raises the right arm, which holds the blaster, to aim: the gear's axle carries a 24-tooth gear driving an 8-tooth gear in the torso, whose 12-tooth bevel gear turns a 20-tooth bevel gear on the right shoulder's axle.
functions.source: book: torso steps 4-8 (bevel gears), backpack steps 13-16 and 20 (pages 42-46); photos on pages 53-55

functions.does: The left arm swings at the shoulder and bends at the elbow, so it can be posed.
functions.source: inferred: arm steps and the photos on pages 47 and 52-53, which show it in different places; the book doesn't say

functions.does: Each leg bends at the knee, and a rubber band across the knee pulls it straight again.
functions.source: inferred: leg steps 8-11 (pages 10-11) hinge the shin to the thigh and put a rubber band across; the book doesn't show the knee bending
functions.note: the rubber band only matters under force; whether the knees are meant to bend is unsure

functions.does: The blaster is held in the right hand by a magnet, so it can be taken out and put back.
functions.source: book: arm step 12 (magnet holder) and the blaster steps (page 37)
